record.paper_title: Four nucleon systems: a zoom to the open problems in nuclear interaction
record.context_brief: Three-nucleon forces versus nonlocal two-nucleon off-shell effects
record.original_question: How can few-nucleon nuclear interaction models be constrained so that one can determine whether missing physics in systems with more than two nucleons should be represented as explicit three-nucleon forces or instead absorbed into nonlocal two-nucleon off-shell terms? Binding energies of light nuclei alone are insufficient because low-energy few-nucleon binding depends on very few parameters and can be fitted by adding three-nucleon forces or by changing nonlocal two-body interactions; the needed constraints should come from continuum observables, such as four-nucleon thresholds and resonances, that test different spatial configurations.

evidence.quote: A standard practice to account for the missing off-shell physics in description of N>2 nuclei is implementation of 3N forces. In such a manner it is not difficult to improve description of 3N and 4N binding energies. However such procedure, which relies only on good description of binding energies can be quite misleading.
Thus study of nuclear binding energies, even being of fundamental importance, can provide only very limited information on nuclear interaction structure.

One thus could expect that a substantial part of 3- and multi-nucleon forces could also be absorbed by nonlocal terms. A considerable simplification would result if the bulk of experimental data could be described by only using two-body nonlocal interaction.
Only careful analysis of continuum spectra, which enables one to test various space configurations, can impose stronger constrains to the off-shell structure of the nuclear interaction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an A-nucleon quantum mechanical Hamiltonian of the form
H = sum_{i=1}^{A} T_i + sum_{i<j} V_{ij} + sum_{i<j<k} W_{ijk},
where T_i is the kinetic energy of nucleon i, V_{ij} is a two-nucleon potential (possibly nonlocal, i.e. an integral operator with kernel V(r,r') rather than a multiplication operator V(r) delta(r-r')), and W_{ijk} is an explicit three-nucleon force. Two two-nucleon potentials V and V' are called phase-equivalent if they produce identical NN scattering phase shifts and identical deuteron binding for all energies; such potentials may nevertheless differ off the energy shell and yield different predictions for A >= 3 systems.

It is known that for A = 3, 4 the low-energy binding energies depend on only a small number of effective parameters, so that any discrepancy between a two-nucleon-only prediction and experiment can be repaired either by (i) adding a three-nucleon force W_{ijk} fitted to the binding energies, or (ii) replacing V_{ij} by a phase-equivalent nonlocal two-nucleon potential V'_{ij} with different off-shell behavior. Thus binding energies alone cannot distinguish genuine three-nucleon forces from nonlocal two-nucleon off-shell effects.

Problem. Identify a set of continuum observables in the four-nucleon system (for instance, positions and widths of the low-lying resonances and thresholds in the 4N continuum, and elastic and reaction cross sections in n+³H, p+³He, d+d channels) and prove or disprove the following:

(a) There exist observables O_1, ..., O_k among these continuum quantities such that, for any two Hamiltonians H and H' that reproduce all NN scattering data, the deuteron, and the experimental ³H and ⁴He binding energies, requiring O_j(H) = O_j(H') for j = 1,...,k forces the three-nucleon-force parts of H and H' to be related to the nonlocal off-shell parts of V_{ij} and V'_{ij} in a uniquely determined way (i.e. the ambiguity between "explicit 3N force" and "nonlocal 2N off-shell content" is removed by these observables).

(b) Quantify the minimal k and exhibit explicit observables achieving (a), or prove that no finite set of such continuum observables suffices.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of distinguishing explicit three-nucleon forces from nonlocal two-nucleon off-shell effects via four-nucleon continuum observables remains an active open research program. Subsequent work on 4N scattering (n-³H, p-³He, d-d) and reviews of chiral 3N forces continue to treat the disentanglement of 3NF effects from off-shell 2N ambiguities as an unsolved issue, with progress but no definitive resolution.

status_evidence.title: Four-nucleon scattering: A testing ground for nuclear forces
status_evidence.snippet: Four-nucleon reactions provide stringent tests of nuclear Hamiltonians, including 3N force effects; several discrepancies remain unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: 4N continuum observables are still being used to constrain 3N forces; problem ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Three-nucleon forces: from cold nuclei to neutron stars
status_evidence.snippet: The role of 3NFs and their off-shell ambiguity with 2N interactions is a continuing area of investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Off-shell/3NF ambiguity remains an open problem in nuclear interaction studies.
